partner_context.their_ambition: You are the #2 US rideshare platform and, since the 2025 FreeNow acquisition, a global multi-mobility company operating in 11 countries and nearly 1,000 cities — rideshare and taxis across North America and Europe, plus bikeshare (Citi Bike, Bay Wheels, Bluebikes) through Lyft Urban Solutions. Your purpose is 'to serve and connect,' and your growth thesis is multimodal: own more of the trip, in more modes, in more cities.
partner_context.their_pressure: Your core US market is dense, contested and maturing on land, and your new European footprint via FreeNow needs differentiated modes to win against entrenched incumbents. Your most water-defined American markets — New York, Miami, the Bay Area, Seattle, Boston — are hemmed in by congested bridges, causeways and ferry queues, and your marquee European markets (Greece, Italy, Spain) are built around islands and coasts no rideshare app has ever served on the water.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Water is the multimodal mode you don't yet run — and it sits in the middle of your densest markets. Navier turns it into a tier in your app: a software-defined foiling fleet, booked in Lyft (and FreeNow), stitched to Citi Bike, Bay Wheels and Bluebikes at the pier, on the congested water corridors of your biggest US cities and the iconic island geographies of your new European frontier — the same network model already ramping at scale in the Maldives.

hero.title: Lyft × Navier — the multimodal platform, on the water
hero.subtitle: From New York's rivers to the Cyclades — Lyft already owns the rides and the bikes. Water is the mode no one runs yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch a Lyft-branded foiling water tier across the most water-defined cities in Lyft's network — booked in-app, stitched to Citi Bike, Bay Wheels and Bluebikes, premium-priced, and proven to travel from the US to the new European FreeNow frontier. Navier brings the software-defined hydrofoiling fleet and the network playbook now proven in the Maldives; Lyft brings the demand, the app, the bikes, and a 1,000-city multimodal map. Together we turn congested bridge-and-tunnel crossings and slow ferry slogs into fast, smooth, on-demand water trips — and claim the category as a new multimodal mode.

why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, dramatically more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging-infrastructure dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026); NYC Ferry and WETA prove Americans will commute by water; and Lyft's 2025 FreeNow acquisition just put the iconic island geographies of Europe inside its app. The category gets claimed cluster-by-cluster — and Lyft's most congested US waters and its new European coasts are the surfaces that matter.
multimodal_fit: Lyft already runs the hardest parts: real-time demand, dispatch, dynamic pricing, and — uniquely — the bikeshare networks (Citi Bike, Bay Wheels, Bluebikes) sitting at the waterfront in its biggest cities. A foiling water tier slots straight in: same app, captain-partners alongside driver-partners, the water leg booked door-to-door with a bike or a ride to and from the pier. Navier is the missing mode in a multimodal map Lyft already operates across 1,000 cities.

differentiation.why_navier: Software-defined and autonomy-ready — the same software-first, multimodal instincts you bring. A factory in Turkey for supply, a ~100-vessel at-scale network already proving the model in the Maldives, and a two-platform fleet (Pioneer II for harbours, Quanta-LR for the offshore runs) that fits both your dense US bays and your new European island geographies.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged for Lyft: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out); a ~100-vessel network is ramping in the Maldives; and the 2025 FreeNow acquisition just doubled Lyft's map — putting both America's most congested waters and Europe's iconic islands inside one multimodal app, with the bikes already at the docks.

This is the water layer of Lyft's biggest market: an in-app foiling tier that turns the rivers and the harbour into a fast, smooth commuter and leisure spine, integrated with the rides and bikes Lyft already runs across the five boroughs.

Today the cross-sound commute means long waits in car-ferry queues. This is the water layer of Lyft's Seattle market: an in-app foiling tier that turns the cross-sound commute into a fast passenger hop and opens a Quanta-LR run to the San Juans and Victoria.

markets.label: Athens & the Cyclades

Through the FreeNow acquisition (completed July 2025), Lyft now operates across nine European countries and 180+ cities — and Greece is its marquee water market. The Saronic Gulf rings Athens with islands (Aegina, Hydra, Poros, Spetses) and the Cyclades — Mykonos, Santorini, Paros and dozens more — are the most iconic island-hopping geography on earth, served today by slow, crowded, weather-cancelled diesel ferries. This is the proof that Lyft's water tier travels: an in-app foiling layer on the Saronic commute and a Quanta-LR Cyclades network, distributed through FreeNow.

proof_points.claim: The vessel is commercial today in the US.
proof_points.evidence: The N30 Pioneer II is in commercial service now — 70 nm range, ~30 kt, 6–8 passengers — already operating with the Four Seasons on Lake Austin. A US-proven, delivery-ready platform.

proof_points.claim: A network at scale is already being built.
proof_points.evidence: Navier is ramping a roughly 100-vessel water network in the Maldives with JIH Global over three years and signed a national agreement with WorldBridge in Cambodia in May 2026.

proof_points.claim: Multimodal is Lyft's stated growth thesis.
proof_points.evidence: Lyft's purpose is 'to serve and connect,' and its growth strategy is to own more of the trip in more modes. A foiling water tier is the next mode — the one no rideshare platform has yet.

objections.concern: Is there enough water distance in US cities to matter?
objections.response: The value isn't distance — it's the bridge and tunnel congestion the water bypasses. Wall St↔LIC is 2 nm of water versus a packed subway transfer; Miami↔South Beach is 3 nm versus causeway gridlock. Short hops win precisely because the road alternative is so slow.

objections.concern: Range for the longer runs (Hamptons, Cyclades)?
objections.response: The Quanta-LR hybrid covers up to 700 nm with no charging infrastructure, handling Manhattan↔Montauk (~95 nm) and Piraeus↔Saronic (~30 nm). The dense intra-city hops sit comfortably inside the all-electric Pioneer II envelope.

objections.concern: US marine regulation is strict — is the path real?
objections.response: We launch on existing berths and ferry corridors, market by market, with a first-of-class certification path. No new infrastructure or rights-of-way; each city is a self-contained pilot.

objections.concern: Why would Lyft add boats it doesn't operate?
objections.response: You don't operate them. Navier brings the fleet, captains and maintenance; Lyft brings demand, dispatch, the wallet and the brand — the same model as cars and bikes, extended to the water.

end_state.headline: The water layer of North America's multimodal platform — and FreeNow's coasts in Europe.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every waterfront market Lyft and FreeNow already serve — New York's rivers and the East End, Miami and South Florida, San Francisco Bay, Puget Sound, Boston Harbor and New England, and the Athenian Riviera and Cyclades.

steady_state.total_markets: 6+ coastal clusters across North America & Europe
steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II commute capillaries + Quanta-LR coastal and island legs
steady_state.tam_framing: Tens of millions of bridge-bound and island-bound trips a year, today lost to congestion and timetables, moved into the Lyft app.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is the waterfront map of Lyft's footprint. Start where the bridges are worst — New York and Miami — prove the in-app water tier, then extend across the Bay, Puget Sound, Boston and the FreeNow coasts of the Mediterranean.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet (Pioneer II + Quanta-LR), captain training, maintenance and the network operating system.
the_ask.partner_brings: Demand and dispatch through the Lyft / FreeNow app, the wallet, the brand, and the choice of launch city.
the_ask.next_step: Scope a first pilot in one flagship city — New York or Miami — co-defining the in-app water tier on three corridors.

close.title: One app. Rides, bikes — and now the water.
close.body: Lyft already owns the trip on land in America's waterfront cities. Water is the one mode no rideshare platform has added. Start where the bridges are worst, prove the foiling tier, and make the river crossing as easy to book as a car.
